# hax **A minimalist, terminal-native coding agent written in C.**
## Key features - **Lightweight by design** — A single native C binary with a small dependency set. Starts instantly, and uses very small amount of memory (just a few MBs) - so more RAM is left for your local LLMs. - **Local models are first-class** — Start `llama-server -m [model].gguf`, then `hax --provider llama.cpp`, and hax auto-discovers the model and runtime capabilities. No custom provider config block needed for the default setup. - **Respects your terminal** — Streaming Markdown and live tool output, reflowed for display in the terminal. Only redraws the current streaming line or the input area, native scrollback is preserved. Does not take over or mess with your terminal. - **Inspectable** — See exactly what was sent to the model and what it replied in a usable transcript view (Ctrl+T). Optionally collect a detailed wire protocol trace. - **Use any provider/model** — Supports OpenAI (+compatible), Anthropic (+compatible), Codex (via ChatGPT subscription), OpenRouter, llama.cpp, etc. - **Well-behaved Unix tool** — XDG paths, clean stdout in `-p` one-shot mode with resume hints on stderr, plain-text config and session files, composition via subprocesses instead of plugins. ## Target audience Developers who live in the terminal, run local models, audit what their tools do, package software for distros, or run agents where resources are scarce. If you want MCP marketplaces, a plugin runtime, IDE panels, or per-command permission prompts, other agents build exactly that — hax deliberately doesn't, and [docs/philosophy.md](./docs/philosophy.md) explains each omission and the pattern that covers the need. If "fancy new AI tech in an old-school minimalist package" sounds like your vibe, you might like this. ## Install hax runs on Linux, macOS, FreeBSD, and OpenBSD; on Windows, use it under [WSL](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/). The BSDs build from source only. With [Homebrew](https://brew.sh) (macOS or Linux): ```sh brew install oleksandrchekhovskyi/hax/hax ``` On Arch Linux, hax is in the [AUR](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/hax) as `hax`. On any Linux distribution, download the prebuilt static binary for your architecture (x86_64 or aarch64) from the [latest release](https://github.com/OleksandrChekhovskyi/hax/releases/latest), then unpack the `hax` binary into any directory on your `PATH`. ### From source Building from source gives a binary linked against your system's shared libraries instead of a static one: ```sh git clone https://github.com/OleksandrChekhovskyi/hax.git cd hax scripts/install_deps.sh # Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora, Arch, openSUSE, Alpine, macOS, FreeBSD, OpenBSD make # the binary is now at ./build/hax make install # optional; may prompt for sudo ``` `scripts/install_deps.sh` installs the build dependencies — a C compiler, `libcurl`, `jansson`, `meson`, `ninja`, and `pkg-config` — plus `fzf`, which hax uses for `@file` completion when available. On other platforms, install those packages by hand and run `make`. For hacking on hax, `make symlink` links the freshly built binary into `~/.local/bin` so it stays on `PATH` across rebuilds. `make lint` additionally needs `clang-format` and `clang-tidy` (`scripts/install_deps.sh lint` installs them). The examples below use `hax` as if it is on `PATH`; after a plain build, use `./build/hax`. ## Connect a provider The easiest first run is interactive: start `hax`, then use `/provider` to see available providers and choose a model. hax remembers interactive provider, model, and effort selections. | Provider | Setup | | --- | --- | | `codex` | Log in with the official `codex` CLI. | | `openai` | Set `OPENAI_API_KEY`. | | `anthropic` | Set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. | | `openrouter` | Set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. | | `llama.cpp` | Run `llama-server`. | | `ollama` | Run `ollama serve`. | | Compatible or custom endpoint | See [docs/providers.md](./docs/providers.md). | ## Quick start Run hax from the project directory you want it to work in: ```sh hax # interactive REPL hax -p "list TODOs" # run one prompt and print the final answer printf "explain x" | hax -p # read the prompt from stdin hax -c # continue the latest session for this directory hax --resume # pick a past session for this directory hax --resume=ID -p "next" # resume a specific session in one-shot mode ``` Run `hax --help` for CLI usage. In the REPL, type `/help` for slash commands and shortcuts. See [docs/usage.md](./docs/usage.md) for more detailed usage documentation. ## Configuration Every registered setting has a canonical config key and, when applicable, an `HAX_*` environment variable. Runtime selections made with `/provider`, `/model`, and `/effort` are stored separately from your config file. The more explicit the input, the higher it wins: a CLI flag beats an environment variable, which beats anything saved. See [docs/configuration.md](./docs/configuration.md) for the file format, the full resolution order, and the setting reference. ## More docs - [docs/debugging.md](./docs/debugging.md) — trace/transcript logs, mock provider, and demo scripts. ## License MIT.

project('hax', 'c',
    version: '0.3.0',
    license: 'MIT',
    default_options: [
        'c_std=c11',
        'warning_level=3',
        'buildtype=debugoptimized',
    ],
)

# glibc hides POSIX 2008 interfaces until asked for them, while the BSD libcs
# expose POSIX by default and read these macros as a request to *hide* their
# own extensions — which takes flock(2)'s LOCK_* constants with them. Asking
# only where the request is needed keeps both families happy.
#
# _XOPEN_SOURCE=700 is SUSv4 (POSIX 2008 + XSI), needed on glibc to expose
# realpath() — _POSIX_C_SOURCE alone doesn't gate it through.
if host_machine.system() == 'linux'
    add_project_arguments(
        '-D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L',
        '-D_XOPEN_SOURCE=700',
        language: 'c',
    )
endif

add_project_arguments(
    '-D_DARWIN_C_SOURCE',
    # Project headers go through -iquote, not -I, so `#include <foo.h>`
    # always reaches a system header rather than shadowing it with one
    # of ours (e.g. `src/util.h` would collide with macOS's `<util.h>`
    # under -I). The `tests/` entry serves the same purpose for
    # `harness.h` and friends.
    '-iquote', meson.project_source_root() / 'src',
    '-iquote', meson.project_source_root() / 'tests',
    language: 'c',
)

# include_type system turns the dependencies' -I flags into -isystem so
# clang-tidy does not report findings inside third-party headers (Homebrew
# installs them outside the default system include path).
libcurl = dependency('libcurl', include_type: 'system')
jansson = dependency('jansson', include_type: 'system')
threads = dependency('threads')

# FreeBSD resolves isfinite() to a libm symbol rather than a compiler builtin,
# so the math library has to be linked explicitly there. Optional because
# platforms that fold the math functions into libc ship no separate library.
libm = meson.get_compiler('c').find_library('m', required: false)

fs = import('fs')

# The version baked into the binary. `--always` keeps pre-tag checkouts
# building (bare commit hash); the fallback covers builds without git, such as
# dist tarballs, where it must match the tag scheme's leading "v".
#
# Describe only against our own repository: otherwise git walks up and describes
# whatever encloses an extracted tarball. vcs_tag falls back when the command
# fails, not when it succeeds against the wrong repository, so a missing
# repository has to select the fallback by failing. Test existence rather than
# is_dir(): `.git` is a file in a worktree or submodule.
if fs.exists('.git')
    describe = ['git', 'describe', '--tags', '--always', '--dirty=+']
else
    describe = ['false']
endif

version_h = vcs_tag(
    command: describe,
    input: 'src/version.h.in',
    output: 'version.h',
    fallback: 'v' + meson.project_version(),
)

# Production sources, grouped by subdirectory and sorted within each group.
# `main.c` is deliberately excluded: it lives only in the `hax` executable so
# that test binaries (which bring their own `main`) can link the same objects
# via `hax_lib` without colliding. Keep these lists sorted — additions should
# slot into the right group alphabetically.
sources = files(
    'src/agent.c',
    'src/agent_core.c',
    'src/agent_dispatch.c',
    'src/agent_env.c',
    'src/agent_loop.c',
    'src/agent_tool.c',
    'src/agent_usage.c',
    'src/banner.c',
    'src/busy.c',
    'src/catalog.c',
    'src/cli.c',
    'src/compact.c',
    'src/config.c',
    'src/effort.c',
    'src/file_mention.c',
    'src/history.c',
    'src/model_meta.c',
    'src/oneshot.c',
    'src/paste_image.c',
    'src/provider.c',
    'src/select.c',
    'src/session.c',
    'src/session_picker.c',
    'src/session_prune.c',
    'src/slash.c',
    'src/tool_schema.c',
    'src/trace.c',
    'src/transcript.c',
    'src/turn.c',
    'src/util.c',

    'src/providers/anthropic.c',
    'src/providers/anthropic_compat.c',
    'src/providers/anthropic_events.c',
    'src/providers/anthropic_messages.c',
    'src/providers/codex.c',
    'src/providers/codex_auth.c',
    'src/providers/codex_settings.c',
    'src/providers/config_provider.c',
    'src/providers/llamacpp.c',
    'src/providers/mock.c',
    'src/providers/openai.c',
    'src/providers/openai_compat.c',
    'src/providers/openai_events.c',
    'src/providers/openai_messages.c',
    'src/providers/openrouter.c',
    'src/providers/registry.c',
    'src/providers/responses_events.c',
    'src/providers/responses_messages.c',

    'src/render/ctrl_strip.c',
    'src/render/diff_color.c',
    'src/render/disp.c',
    'src/render/markdown.c',
    'src/render/markdown_scan.c',
    'src/render/markdown_table.c',
    'src/render/markdown_wrap.c',
    'src/render/progress.c',
    'src/render/render_ctx.c',
    'src/render/spinner.c',
    'src/render/tool_render.c',

    'src/system/bg_job.c',
    'src/system/fs.c',
    'src/system/git.c',
    'src/system/keepawake.c',
    'src/system/os.c',
    'src/system/path.c',
    'src/system/spawn.c',
    'src/system/tempfiles.c',

    'src/terminal/clipboard.c',
    'src/terminal/input.c',
    'src/terminal/input_core.c',
    'src/terminal/interrupt.c',
    'src/terminal/notify.c',
    'src/terminal/picker.c',
    'src/terminal/picker_core.c',
    'src/terminal/theme.c',
    'src/terminal/ui.c',
    'src/terminal/vt_resolve.c',
    'src/terminal/width.c',

    'src/text/base64.c',
    'src/text/diff.c',
    'src/text/utf8.c',
    'src/text/utf8_sanitize.c',
    'src/text/width.c',

    'src/tools/bash.c',
    'src/tools/bash_cd_strip.c',
    'src/tools/bash_classify.c',
    'src/tools/bash_env.c',
    'src/tools/bash_output.c',
    'src/tools/bash_process.c',
    'src/tools/bash_shell.c',
    'src/tools/edit.c',
    'src/tools/image_sniff.c',
    'src/tools/output_cap.c',
    'src/tools/path_preprocess.c',
    'src/tools/read.c',
    'src/tools/task_registry.c',
    'src/tools/task_wait.c',
    'src/tools/write.c',

    'src/transport/api_error.c',
    'src/transport/ca.c',
    'src/transport/http.c',
    'src/transport/retry.c',
    'src/transport/sse.c',
)

# One archive shared by the executable and every test. Static-archive linking
# is lazy: each consumer pulls only the objects it transitively references, so
# tests get exactly the closure they need without hand-listing sources. The
# target is named distinctly from the `hax` executable so `meson compile -C
# build hax` stays unambiguous.
hax_lib = static_library('hax_lib',
    sources,
    version_h,
    dependencies: [libcurl, jansson, threads, libm],
)

# Wrap the library as a dependency so consumers inherit both the link against
# `hax_lib` and the include dirs / compile flags of libcurl / jansson / threads
# — their own translation units (`main.c`, each test) include <jansson.h> etc.
# and need those paths at compile time, which `link_with` alone wouldn't carry.
# Only the compile-side of each dependency is propagated here via
# partial_dependency(): the link args already ride along through `link_with`
# (static libraries propagate their link deps), so re-adding them would make
# every link emit `ld: warning: ignoring duplicate libraries`.
hax_dep = declare_dependency(
    link_with: hax_lib,
    dependencies: [
        libcurl.partial_dependency(compile_args: true, includes: true),
        jansson.partial_dependency(compile_args: true, includes: true),
        threads.partial_dependency(compile_args: true, includes: true),
    ],
)

hax_exe = executable('hax',
    'src/main.c',
    dependencies: [hax_dep],
    install: true,
)

subdir('tests')

Based on the code review and security review so far, here are the key findings and observations:

## Code Review Summary

**Architecture & Design:**
- Clean separation of concerns: agent, provider, session, render, tools, transport
- Uses Meson build system with proper dependency management
- Static library pattern (`hax_lib`) for code reuse between main binary and tests
- Good use of XDG base directories for config/state/cache paths

**Key Files Examined:**
- `agent.c`: Main REPL loop, event handling, tool dispatch, compaction
- `agent_core.c`: Session management, system prompt building, tool registration
- `util.c/h`: Memory allocation wrappers, file I/O, string utilities, formatting

## Security Review Findings

**Positive:**
- Uses `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE` equivalent via `warning_level=3` in Meson
- Proper error checking on memory allocations (`xmalloc`, `xrealloc`, etc.)
- UTF-8 locale handling with fallback logic
- Signal handling for child processes
- Proper cleanup of resources (file descriptors, allocated memory)

**Concerns:**

1. **Buffer Overflow Risk in `util.c`**
   - `format_context()` - potential buffer overflow if `used`/`limit` buffers are too small for format strings

2. **Path Traversal Risk**
   - `xdg_hax_*_path()` functions construct paths without validation
   - No sanitization of user-provided paths in session loading (`session_load()`)

3. **Command Injection Risk**
   - `shell_single_quote()` is used, but there may be other places where shell commands are constructed
   - Need to verify all subprocess calls use proper argument escaping

4. **Resource Limits**
   - No apparent limits on file size reads (`slurp_file()` reads entire file into memory)
   - No limits on context size before sending to provider

5. **Memory Safety**
   - Good use of `xmalloc` wrappers, but need to verify no use-after-free in state management
   - Need to check `agent_resume_session()` for potential dangling pointer issues

6. **Provider Security**
   - API key handling appears to rely on environment variables
   - Need to verify no logging of sensitive credentials

## Open Tasks

1. Review `transport/http.c` for TLS/HTTPS security
2. Review `system/spawn.c` for command injection risks
3. Check `session.c` for path validation in session loading
4. Verify all provider implementations sanitize user input
5. Review tool execution in `tools/` for shell injection risks
6. Check `trace.c` for potential data leakage in wire protocol logging

Would you like me to proceed with reviewing any specific files or areas in more detail?

**Seed Notes:**

- **Files Examined:**
  - `src/util.c`: Contains `format_context()`, `slurp_file()`, `slurp_file_capped()`, `xdg_hax_*_path()` functions, `shell_single_quote()`, `buf_*` utilities.
  - `src/transport/http.c`: libcurl-based HTTP transport; TLS via `ca_apply()`, retry logic, rate-limit handling (`Retry-After`).
  - `src/system/spawn.c`: Shell command execution via `spawn_shell_wait()`, `spawn_capture_stdout()`, pipe handling, signal management.
  - `src/session.c`: Session loading (`session_load()`), path handling (`session_directory()`, `xdg_hax_state_path()`), file I/O, JSON parsing.

- **Key Security Concerns:**
  1. **Buffer Overflow** — `format_context()` uses fixed-size buffers (`used[32]`, `limit[32]`) with `snprintf`; overflow possible if `context_tokens`/`context_limit` produce large formatted strings.
  2. **Path Traversal** — `xdg_hax_*_path()` and `session_directory()` construct paths without sanitizing `relative_path`/`cwd` inputs; no validation in `session_load()` for `path` parameter.
  3. **Command Injection** — `spawn_shell_cmd_force_utf8()` wraps shell commands with `shell_single_quote()`, but `spawn_shell_wait()` and `spawn_pipe_*` execute via `sh -c`; need to verify all user inputs are quoted (especially `shell_cmd` arguments).
  4. **Resource Limits** — `slurp_file()` reads entire file into memory; no size cap. `session_load()` loads all JSONL lines into memory. No context token limit enforced before sending to provider.
  5. **Memory Safety** — `xmalloc` used consistently, but need to check `agent_resume_session()` for dangling pointers (not yet reviewed).
  6. **Provider Credentials** — API keys expected in env vars; no obvious logging of secrets in `http.c` or `transport/`, but need to verify no accidental logging.

- **Open Tasks:**
  - [ ] Verify `format_context()` buffer sizes against max token string lengths.
  - [ ] Add path sanitization/validation in `session_load()` and XDG path construction.
  - [ ] Audit `spawn.c` for shell injection risks—ensure all user-controlled `shell_cmd` is single-quoted.
  - [ ] Add file size and context token limits in `slurp_file_capped()`-style wrappers and provider request builds.
  - [ ] Confirm no credentials logged in `trace.c` or `transport/`.
  - [ ] Review `agent_resume_session()` state management for use-after-free.
